passage: The photo was from the school picnic at the dam outside Hoshangabad: Meenu asleep on the bus, mouth open, a crisp stuck to her cheek. Kunal had taken it and sent it to Bhavna. 'Put it in the class group, it's hilarious,' he wrote. So she did. By evening it had gone round the whole school and to a cousin in the next town. Meenu didn't come to school the next day. When the principal called Bhavna and Kunal to the office, Bhavna said at once, 'Kunal told me to send it. I just did what he said.' Kunal said, 'I only sent it to you. She's the one who posted it.' The principal looked from one to the other. 'Each of you pressed send. The counsellor is visiting Meenu's home today. Now, who is going to help fix this?'

qa.q: Where was Meenu when the photo was taken?
qa.a: Meenu was asleep on the bus from the school picnic.

qa.q: Why did Bhavna say 'I just did what he said' at once?
qa.a: Pointing to Kunal's instruction made Bhavna feel less responsible for the harm, as if the choice to post it belonged to him.

qa.q: What did the principal say that cut through the blame, and why?
qa.a: 'Each of you pressed send' made both see their own action, and asking who would help fix it turned blame into repair for Meenu.

qa.q: What has the photo been like for Meenu?
qa.a: For Meenu it has been deeply embarrassing: the whole school and beyond saw it, and she stayed home the next day.

grounding: Shows a teenager who spreads an embarrassing photo of a classmate and says a friend told her to, while the classmate's hurt grows.

subtopic: Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility
passage: In the changing room after PE at their school in Valencia, Layla showed Sofia a video on her phone: Mateo slipping on the wet floor and landing in the mop bucket, arms flailing. 'Post it on the class story,' Layla said. 'You've got more followers. Go on.' Sofia hesitated for about two seconds, then posted it. By lunch it had three hundred views and someone had added a clown sticker. Mateo sat in the library all afternoon. When their tutor, Señora Ruiz, called Sofia in, Sofia said, 'Layla told me to. It was her video. I just did what she asked.' Señora Ruiz said, 'Layla asked. You decided. Both are true.' She had Sofia delete it in front of her, and said she had already phoned Mateo's parents and the school counsellor. 'Now,' she said, 'what will you say to Mateo?'

qa.q: How many views did the video have by lunch?
qa.a: By lunch it had three hundred views.

qa.q: Why did Sofia say 'I just did what she asked'?
qa.a: Putting the choice on Layla made Sofia feel less to blame, as if following a friend's request meant the harm wasn't really hers.

qa.q: What did Señora Ruiz do that helped both Mateo and Sofia?
qa.a: She named both parts plainly, had the video deleted, told Mateo's parents and the counsellor, and asked Sofia to plan an apology, so the harm stopped and the choice was owned.

qa.q: What was the afternoon like for Mateo?
qa.a: Mateo hid in the library all afternoon, probably feeling humiliated while hundreds of people watched his fall with a clown sticker on it.

grounding: Shows a teenager who posts an embarrassing video of a classmate and says a friend asked her to, until a tutor separates the asking from the choosing.

subtopic: Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility
passage: At the district hockey club, after the under-16 final, the goalkeeper, Nandita, sat crying on the bench with her helmet off. Aditi, the captain, nudged Zainab. 'Take a pic. For the team group. She's such a baby.' Zainab took it and sent it. Within an hour it was in two other clubs' groups with laughing captions. The next morning Coach called Zainab and Aditi into the office. Zainab spoke first. 'Aditi's captain. She told me to. I was only doing what I was told.' Aditi said, 'I didn't make you.' Coach put Zainab's phone on the desk, the photo on the screen. 'Whose thumb pressed send?' Zainab looked at it a long time. 'Mine.' Coach said Nandita's parents had been told and the club counsellor would sit with Nandita that afternoon. 'You two will help take it down from every group. Then we talk about an apology.'

qa.q: What was Nandita doing when the photo was taken?
qa.a: Nandita sat crying on the bench with her helmet off.

qa.q: Why did Zainab say 'I was only doing what I was told'?
qa.a: Zainab felt ashamed and wanted to escape the blame, so pointing to Aditi as captain made the harm seem to belong to someone with more authority.

qa.q: What did Coach's question 'Whose thumb pressed send?' do?
qa.a: It moved the focus from who asked to who acted, and Zainab admitted 'Mine', the first step towards removing the photo and apologising.

qa.q: How might Nandita feel seeing the photo in other clubs' groups?
qa.a: Nandita would likely feel humiliated and let down by her own team, after already being upset about the final.

grounding: Shows a teenager who shares a photo of a crying teammate and blames the captain's instruction, until a coach asks whose thumb pressed send.

subtopic: Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility
passage:
Subject: About the photo of Ira

Dear Mrs Fernandes,
You asked me to write down what happened, so here it is.
On Tuesday at the science fair, Tamanna took a photo of Ira mid-sneeze, braces showing, glasses slipping. Tamanna is house captain, and she said, 'Send it to the Class 10 group, it's hilarious.' So I sent it. I didn't take it and I didn't write the caption. I only forwarded it because she told me to.
I know Ira didn't come to school on Wednesday or Thursday. But I think Tamanna and the forty people who reacted should be asked about that too, not only me.
Honestly, when a house captain tells you something, you don't really argue.
I keep checking whether Ira has seen the group.
Aadhya, 10B

qa.q: According to Aadhya, who gave the instruction to send the photo?
qa.a: Tamanna, the house captain, who said, 'Send it to the Class 10 group, it's hilarious.'

qa.q: Why does forwarding the photo feel reasonable to Aadhya from the inside?
qa.a: Aadhya feels uneasy, still checking whether Ira has seen the group, but since Tamanna took the photo and gave the order, Aadhya's own part feels like just going along.

qa.q: What choice could Aadhya make now that would actually help Ira?
qa.a: Aadhya could own the one step that was Aadhya's, pressing send, then ask the group to delete the photo and apologise to Ira directly.

qa.q: How might Ira see the question of who 'only' forwarded the photo?
qa.a: For Ira it hardly matters who took it or who gave the order; every forward spread the sneeze photo further, and Ira stayed away from school for two days after it.

grounding: A teenager who spread an embarrassing photo writes that the house captain told them to send it, placing the responsibility on the person in charge.

subtopic: Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility
passage:
Damini, just listen before you say anything. Okay? So at maths tuition on Saturday, Pranav fell asleep on his notebook, mouth open, ink on his cheek. Jaggu clicked a photo and goes, 'Tanvir, forward it to the tuition group, all sixty.' Jaggu's the oldest; sir leaves him in charge when he steps out. So I did. I didn't take it. I didn't write 'sleeping beauty' on it, Jaggu did that.
Now Pranav's mum has called sir, and everyone's saying it was me because it came from my number.
Which is unfair, right? I was only doing what I was told. If Jaggu had said don't, I wouldn't have.
Why are you quiet?
Okay. Okay. Yes, it was my thumb that pressed send. Not Jaggu's.

qa.q: What did Jaggu write on the photo of Pranav?
qa.a: Jaggu wrote 'sleeping beauty' on it.

qa.q: Why does Tanvir feel it is unfair to be blamed?
qa.a: Tanvir feels wronged and defensive, believing the fault belongs to Jaggu, who took the photo, wrote the caption and gave the order as the one left in charge.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Tanvir's story, and what should come next?
qa.a: Damini's silence pushed Tanvir to admit 'it was my thumb that pressed send'; a good next step would be apologising to Pranav and asking the group to delete the photo.

qa.q: How might Pranav feel about the photo, whoever gave the order?
qa.a: Pranav was only asleep, yet sixty people saw the photo; for Pranav it hardly matters who gave the order, because everyone who shared it added to the embarrassment.

grounding: A teenager who forwarded an embarrassing photo insists the older student in charge told them to, before admitting their own part.
